label: Matador Records
description: Vile's fifth album stretches sun-baked slacker rock into sprawling, double-LP length, blending gorgeous fingerpicking with heavy guitar drift. The mood is unhurried and half-stoned, closer to a daydream than a statement. It is the record where his Pavement/Crazy Horse-indebted sound became widescreen.
lineage: Vile was a founding member of The War on Drugs in Philadelphia; his sound here seems descended from Pavement's loose-limbed guitar rock and Neil Young's amp-drone side.

label: Matador Records
description: A more introspective turn with banjo and piano alongside the guitars, led by the single 'Pretty Pimpin'. Vile's cracked, mumbling delivery and stream-of-consciousness lyrics stay pure slacker even as the arrangements soften toward folk.
lineage: Sounds akin to the Pavement-to-Silver Jews thread of deadpan funny-sad songwriting, in a more folk-inflected register.

label: Domino Recording Company
description: Alex Giannascoli's album pairs pitched-up vocal tics and Auto-Tune warps with plainspoken, sometimes menacing songwriting about faith and small-town life. Gentle acoustic arrangements and gospel-tinged hooks sit next to eerie, lo-fi textures. It suits listeners who like songs that are tender and unsettling at once.
lineage: Grew out of Bandcamp-era home recording; its fragmentary lo-fi songcraft sounds indebted to Guided by Voices and Elliott Smith.

label: RCA Records
description: Alex G's major-label debut keeps his warped, intimate production but pushes toward higher fidelity. Latter-day R.E.M. and Daniel Johnston echoes are folded into the same gentle-menace songwriting that runs through his earlier records, with the title track 'Headlights' as the clearest example.
lineage: Continues Alex G's arc from Bandcamp lo-fi into a wider, still jangle-rooted indie-pop palette.

label: Lame-O Records
description: Matt Scottoline's project turns plainspoken heartbreak into tight, hook-forward power pop recorded with an easy, unfussy jangle. It sits alongside Philadelphia's current power-pop revival, for fans of short, sweet, sad songs.
lineage: Sounds indebted to Big Star and Superchunk, filtered through the Philadelphia DIY scene.

label: Self-released
description: Russell Edling's group turns its own songwriting process inside out across a spacious, nervy set of fuzzed and jangling power pop. Dreamy mellotron cuts against scrubby guitars, with a playful, Elephant 6-style looseness.
lineage: Sounds indebted to Big Star and Elephant 6 melodicism, sitting within Philadelphia's current power-pop scene.
key_tracks: Another Grand Offering for the Swine

label: Lame-O Records
description: Golden Apples' hookiest, most fuzzed-out set is packed with memorable choruses in the power-pop and jangle vein. Distorted guitars and bright melodies push the songs forward without losing their homemade Philadelphia feel.
lineage: Big Star melodicism via Philadelphia's power-pop revival.

label: Matador Records
description: Three young Chicagoans' debut is an efficient romp through indie rock's post-punk and jangle fringes. Interlocking guitars, feedback, and deadpan vocals keep songs short and sharp. It suits listeners who love noisy, tasteful '90s-style indie rock.
lineage: Sounds indebted to Pavement and Sonic Youth's guitar interplay, filtered through Chicago's all-ages DIY scene.

label: Matador Records
description: A more direct second album of ramshackle, perfect pop songs, with grooves and glowing harmonies replacing the debut's noisier fringes. Clean, jangling guitars and deadpan vocals keep the songs short and spare.
lineage: Continues Horsegirl's post-punk and jangle sound, akin to Pavement, toward cleaner pop songwriting.
borderline_note: needs_verification for key_tracks -- no tracklist scraped

label: Self-released
description: A batch of scrappy rock sketches built on Telecaster-driven hooks and guitar charm. The earworm rippers mix Nuggets garage and '90s indie jangle with punk swagger, most of them over in about two minutes.
lineage: Sounds indebted to Nuggets-era garage rock and '90s indie jangle.

label: Self-released
description: Adventurous, stylistically shifting indie rock that still flows front to back, with Built to Spill and Pavement echoes throughout. Jangling guitars stretch into long solos beneath deadpan vocals.
lineage: Sounds indebted to Pavement's loose song-suite structure and Built to Spill's guitar interplay.

label: Rotten Apple
description: A twee-punk-leaning collection of home recordings, full of pristine, thoughtful jangle-pop with big hooks and surging punk energy. Lo-fi fidelity and short songs keep it scrappy and small-town intimate.
lineage: Sounds indebted to Guided by Voices and Beat Happening's DIY-jangle lineage.

label: ANTI-
description: Detroit's Bonny Doon make their ANTI- debut breezier and more accessible than past records, with lyrics that sneak up on the listener over unhurried, conversational arrangements. Close harmonies and hushed, deadpan vocals keep it gentle.
lineage: Slacker-folk that sounds indebted to the Silver Jews and Palace, filtered through Detroit's indie scene.

label: Grand Jury Music
description: Charlie Martin and Will Taylor's duo makes soft-focus, mid-fi slacker pop, warm and unhurried. Plain-spoken affection rides gentle drum-machine pulses and hushed, lullaby-like vocals, for listeners who want indie rock as a quiet comfort.
lineage: Sounds descended from the lo-fi college-radio-to-Bandcamp lineage of Duster and Alex G.

label: Arts & Crafts
description: A long, double-LP-length set with stronger melodies and more hi-fi recording than earlier Hovvdy work. Hushed, lullaby-soft vocals and gentle pulses keep the duo's intimacy intact even as the sound fills out.
lineage: Continues Hovvdy's lo-fi slacker-pop arc toward fuller production.
borderline_note: needs_verification for key_tracks and label -- label from memory (Terry file gives no label), not confirmed on a scraped page

label: Third Man Records
description: Will Anderson's project buries plainspoken, slacker-jangly songwriting under warm shoegaze fuzz and feedback. Cartwheel was his Third Man Records debut, for listeners who like hooks hidden inside a noise wall.
lineage: Sits between shoegaze fuzz and the jangle-pop tradition, sounding indebted to Guided by Voices' song-fragment economy.
borderline_note: Fuzz-heavy sound borders shoegaze (X9); kept as C7 for its jangle/slacker songwriting core per Terry file placement.

label: Seasick Records
description: Loud, relentlessly hooky rock that channels Summerteeth-era Wilco and Ty Segall's frantic energy. Crazy Horse fuzz and Telecaster twang back small-town storytelling at full tilt.
lineage: Sounds indebted to Neil Young & Crazy Horse fuzz, with Wilco's Americana-pop as a touchstone.
borderline_note: Terry file names label as Born Yesterday; Bandcamp page text names Seasick Records as the releasing label -- used the scraped source.

label: Self-released
description: New Orleans slacker-pop trio The Convenience deliver thirteen loose, deadpan-sung tracks built on jangling, lightly lo-fi guitars. The songwriting is plainspoken and wry, closer to a conversation than a performance, in the same Crescent City DIY scene as Lawn.
lineage: Part of New Orleans' current jangle/slacker cluster alongside Lawn.
key_tracks: I Got Exactly What I Wanted

label: Matador Records
description: Will Toledo's first full-band studio album turns Bandcamp-honed bedroom pop into classic-rock-scaled narrative rock, nodding to the Cars, Pavement and Jonathan Richman. It is a sprawling, self-lacerating song cycle of long, anthemic, funny-sad songs.
lineage: Toledo self-released many albums on Bandcamp before signing to Matador; the result sounds fused with Pavement's slacker irony.

album: Sometimes I Sit and Think, and Sometimes I Just Sit
label: Milk! Records
description: Barnett's debut is a wry, rambling slacker-rock landmark, its deadpan run-on lyrics detailing house-hunting anxiety ('Depreston') and open-mic dread ('Pedestrian at Best'). Loose, twangy guitars and a conversational drawl carry the songs.
lineage: Sounds heir to Pavement's talky slacker rock, alongside Australian jangle peers like Dick Diver.

label: Milk! Records
description: A calmer record that trades some of Barnett's wordplay density for spacious, drum-machine-inflected slacker pop. Hushed, breezy arrangements suit its themes of patience and care.
lineage: Barnett's songwriting, which sounds indebted to Pavement, softened toward indie-pop.

label: Matador Records
description: The Brisbane trio add synths and sheen to their jangle-pop, its three songwriters trading plainspoken, bittersweet verses. Close harmonies and deadpan delivery keep it wry and tender.
lineage: Founding member Louis Forster is the son of the Go-Betweens' Robert Forster; the band's jangle sounds descended from the Go-Betweens and Flying Nun.

label: Sub Pop
description: Toronto's Kiwi Jr. sharpen their Pavement- and GBV-descended jangle into a wry, hooky second album. Deadpan vocals trade in pop-culture references and small stories over bright, clipped guitars.
lineage: Sounds directly indebted to Pavement and Guided by Voices.

label: Sub Pop
description: Kiwi Jr.'s third album adds synths and sheen to their wit-and-melody formula, sardonic Toronto indie rock that balances humor and hooks. It builds on the jangle of Cooler Returns and Football Money with a glossier, more synth-lit sound.
lineage: Continues the band's jangle, which sounds descended from Pavement and GBV.

album: On the Intricate Inner Workings of the System
label: Sub Pop
description: The Welsh band's Sub Pop debut is Modern Lovers-meets-Nuggets garage rock with sarcastic dual vocals and clanging riffs. Songs are short, rowdy and funny-sad, often done in under two minutes.
lineage: Sounds indebted to Nuggets garage and the talky deadpan of Jonathan Richman and the Modern Lovers.

label: Self-released
description: A sprawling, hour-long set of relentlessly catchy, fuzz-wrapped garage pop with great dual-singer chemistry. Most songs are short and rowdy, stacking jokes and hooks at speed.
lineage: Continues the band's garage sound, which sounds indebted to Nuggets, at maximalist length.

label: Lame-O Records
description: James Goodson's project crams huge hooks into no-second-wasted power pop, like Fountains of Wayne played at ear-shattering volume. Crazy Horse-style fuzz and anthemic choruses fill short, breathless songs.
lineage: Sounds indebted to Big Star and Fountains of Wayne melodicism, blown out with fuzz-pedal DIY energy.

label: Carpark Records
description: Elizabeth Stokes writes tight, guitar-heavy songs that read as character studies of relationships' aftermaths. Harmonized guitars and anthemic choruses give the heartbreak a bright, driving lift.
lineage: Sounds akin to the New Zealand jangle-pop tradition around Flying Nun, crossed with American power pop.

label: Chapter Music
description: The Melbourne band's debut is loose, plainspoken jangle-pop full of local color and wry deadpan vocals. Drawled, small-town observations sit over relaxed, chiming guitars, a key early record of the 2010s Australian slacker-pop scene.
lineage: Sounds descended from Flying Nun jangle, by way of Melbourne's Chapter Music scene.

label: Self-released
description: A tightly recorded set of plainspoken, jangling Melbourne guitar pop, in the same scene as Dick Diver. Deadpan vocals and short songs keep it brisk and unfussy.
lineage: Sounds descended from Flying Nun jangle, within Melbourne's jangle-pop scene.
